summary: Port native radix shaders and resident contact canonicalization with exact-word contracts and independent stable-sort specifications.
regressions: 93 radix cases cover empty/ragged batches, 255/256/257 and 1023/1024/1025 tails, u32 keys, duplicates, optional auxiliary records, inactive workgroups and guards.
Synthetic 1048577-key histograms exercise two reduction chunks per bin without substituting CPU runtime sorting.
40 canonical cases cover every selector, input permutations, inactive slots, duplicate identities, full-width IDs and all three field schedules.
Both native expected outputs and actual outputs are checked against independent mathematical integer and stable-order specifications, including every scratch word.
differences: The C target serializes each cooperative workgroup phase; GPU targets retain 256 lanes and explicit barriers.
TileLang stores per-lane scatter state in shared storage to use the same phase code for C. This changes scratch placement and is not performance-qualified.
Private prefix temporaries avoid ambiguous Ascend shared-memory read-modify-write barrier insertion. Source lowering alone does not qualify Ascend synchronization.
The standalone sort uses independent batch grids. The native flattened-batch controller optimization is not implemented.

Canonicalization retains native field order but runs all eight 4-bit passes per field, using native three-buffer ping-pong ownership. This preserves ordering but has more dispatches than the variable-bit Rust optimization.
Fixed capacity-bounded launches consume device counters without intermediate host physics/readback. Native indirect grids are also published and checked.

The complete refreshed matrix also accepts the source changes classified separately in records 0031 (inert link guard), 0032 (stable face intersections) and 0033 (analytic collision composition and scoped geometry comparison).
